refuted_claims:
1. Claim: "Admit the family if TPS_F >= 0.80 and |alpha_F| <= 4 points ... a valid family is rejected about 5-10 % of the time." This is recommendation 6, the purpose-1 mechanism.
   - Checked: I reran E5's own e5_tps_sim.py construction (cal-1 cells, n_F = 100, 9 texts, 2,000 draws) and added invalid families.
   - Valid families are rejected 12.7 % of the time under the joint criteria, not 5-10 %.
   - Invalid families admitted:
     - blind to all 6 small-effect texts: 63.8 % with independent per-text noise of SD 2.4 points (66.3 % with shared noise; 31.9 % only if the noise is doubled);
     - small-text responses scrambled: 55.5 %;
     - every contrast exaggerated by x1.46 (E5's own G3 slope): 77.2 %;
     - constant offset of +3.0 points: 68.3 %; of +5.3 points: 32.1 %.
   - Why: the 3 large texts (ids-full, seed-only, control:3) carry the correlation. The gate therefore cannot detect the very failure E5 documents (right on big contrasts, wrong on small ones), and it has no slope criterion.
   - Definitional slip: the report defines alpha_F as a regression intercept, but the code computes mean(family - criterion).

2. Claim: "On the 10 learning-relevant contrasts the Pearson is -0.235 and generated minus real is +5.28 points", hence "Generated items are not yet valid for fine contrasts" (verdict_cn point 6).
   - Checked: results/generated_vs_real.json.
   - The real-item side has a mean SE of 2.83 points against an observed spread of 2.45. It has no reliable variance, so no instrument could correlate with it. The 95 % CI of r at n = 10 is -0.75 to +0.46.
   - Split by solver: on deepseek, the deployment solver (4 contrasts), the gap is +0.6 points and r = +0.57. On the GLM family (6 contrasts) the gap is +8.4.
   - Correct reading: untestable with 74 real items, not "invalid". E5's own rule (calibrate with the deployment solver) argues against pooling GLM contrasts into the headline.

3. Claim: "The parent's p(1-p) predicts which items respond to the task-card text, with AUC 0.85" (verdict_cn point 2: "事先大致能看出来").
   - The number reproduces (0.849), but most of it is mechanical:
     - The trivial flag "not always-pass" already gives 0.821, because an item that passes every run cannot rise by 0.5.
     - Within the 89 non-ceiling items the AUC is 0.744, in-sample.
     - A pure-noise responder set (within-item permutation, 2,000 draws; only 3.5 null responders expected) is "predicted" by the same p(1-p) with median AUC 0.79.
     - The pilot's 2-run version gave 0.514.
   - In the pilot, a same-text comparison (scaffold phase B vs phase A) yields 11 pseudo-responders against ids-full's 27. H6's target was therefore noise-dominated. Its failure says nothing either way, and the rescue ("pooled multi-run strata would work") is untested.
   - "Harm sits in always-pass items" is likewise largely floor/ceiling arithmetic. Its magnitude (-16.5 to -17.7 points) is the informative part.

4. Claim: the MDE table and verdict_cn "按现有题量，能可靠测出的最小泛化效果：SearchQA 6.8、LiveMath 8.2、SpreadsheetBench 9.1、OfficeQA 9.6、ALFWorld 12.2 分".
   - Checked: the size table in section 2 of the coevo5 registration (sizes only; no test pool opened) and E5's dstudy.json components.
   - These are TRAINING panel sizes (200 / 100 / 91 / 74 / 57). Generalisation is evaluated on the evaluation panels (400 / 172 / 125 / ~177 judgeable of 279 / 134). There the population MDE at 2 runs is 3.7 / 6.3 / 7.3 / 6.5 / 8.0 points.
   - Pooled over the registered similar targets, the MDE is ~3.0 points when evolving on OfficeQA (702 target items) and 6.3 when evolving on SearchQA (only OfficeQA is similar).

5. Claim: "a +5-point generalisation claim needs about 220-370 items per benchmark"; learned effects "below every population figure".
   - Every E5 contrast, stratum, tau and pilot arm is against the EMPTY scaffold. cal-1 has no "task card + rule" arm.
   - Cal-1 proxy for an addition on top of the task card (ids-full minus seed-only):
     - tau 0.191;
     - parent run variance 0.027 against 0.053 for the scaffold;
     - n ≈ 196 at 2 runs for a 5-point effect (E5: 374);
     - MDE 4.9 points at 200 items (E5: 6.8).
   - For the owner's actual contrast the requirement is likely about half of E5's figure. The strata also change: with ids-full as parent, 139 of 200 items are always-pass and 30 mixed.

6. Claim: verdict_cn point 8, "泛化得到验证". The pilot replicates task card vs EMPTY scaffold on fresh items of the SAME benchmark. It tests neither cross-benchmark generalisation (the owner's metric), nor a learned rule, nor a rule on top of a good instruction.

7. Claim: verdict_cn point 1, "技能文本主要是在换着题做对，很少整体提高分数".
   - The 1.3 % text share is a share of total variance, which is dominated by item difficulty, and item difficulty cancels in paired contrasts. The task card adds +8.9 points (fresh CI 4.4-13.1).
   - The accurate statement: per-item changes (SD 15.9) are about 3x the mean shift (SD 5.4).
   - "72 % 的差异来自交叉作用" is the share of EXCESS Rasch deviance, not of "the differences". On the probability scale the interaction is about 90 % of text-related variance.

8. Claim: "TPS_F and calibration error over rounds form the verifier's learning curve ... a learnable fitness."
   - Each round's real-side delta is one rule's contrast. In v3 that meant 0-5 discordant items per panel, with nets inside the placebo range.
   - By the reliability arithmetic of item 2, such pairs carry ~zero reliable variance, so the curve would be noise.
   - It is also only selection among fixed families against a fixed criterion. Apart from the stratum steering, nothing in it responds to the Skill side.

9. Claim: IRT "does not fit"; p-IRT and anchor points are "no better than random". Partly refuted.
   - The practical conclusion stands; PromptEval's model is indeed logit-additive.
   - But 2PL slopes from 10-16 respondent texts are unestimable whatever the true structure, and p-IRT and anchors were calibrated on 9 texts instead of the hundreds of models they assume. That is not a fair test of those methods; it only shows they cannot be calibrated here.

10. Minor errors.
    - Signal and Noise has a NeurIPS 2025 version ([NeurIPS](https://neurips.cc/virtual/2025/poster/115712)); the report says "no venue".
    - Truong et al. is ICML 2025, PMLR 267 ([PMLR](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/truong25c.html)), and that abstract says 183 LMs (the report says 172).
    - Fluid Benchmarking is COLM 2025 ([arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.11106)).
    - The family-gate cost is internally inconsistent: about 1,400 cells / 2-4M tokens in section 9, but 2,000 cells / 3-4M in sections 6.3 and 10.
confirmed_claims:
All checks below cost 0 model tokens.

**Reproduced from the raw cal-1 cells (my own ANOVA)**
- Variance split: item 63.8 / text 1.3 / item x text 11.6 / run 23.2 %. SDs 5.4 and 15.9 points.
- Identical-text pair: interaction estimate -0.004, i.e. about 0.
- The arm pass/fail/unknown table.
- Text deltas: ids-full +8.88, seed-only +8.46, control:3 -10.38, cand -3.12, and the rest.
- 25 always-fail and 50 always-pass items over all 44 cal-1 runs.
- Strata 37 / 52 / 111 and every per-stratum net.
- T1 = 27 responders and AUC 0.849, the number itself (the interpretation fails; see refuted item 3).

**E5 analyses that are sound as computed**
- The dead-item analysis is cross-session, not circular: 19 dead and 75 always-pass items, with the stated nets.
- D-study arithmetic reproduces from the stored components: 374 and 122 items; MDE 6.8 and 3.9 points.
- The TPS_F null distribution reproduces: p5 / p50 0.83 / 0.93, slope 0.84.
- The Neyman SDs come from the v3 sessions, not cal-1, so there is no in-sample leakage.

**Pilot E5-P1, recomputed from the 1,800 raw cells on the new machine (read-only)**
- 0 unknown cells; 3,241,924 tokens; strata 41 / 9 / 130.
- ids-full +8.89, control:3 -11.39, cand -8.61 points.
- A2 means -16.54 and -17.69; ids-full net by class 12.5 / 0.5 / 3.0.
- AUC 0.514 and 0.751; scaffold phase-B minus phase-A offset 0.00.
- Drop-A0 bias -6.94 (= -12.5 / 180).

**Other checks**
- Generated SearchQA b06 panel: 111 of 168 items pass every deepseek cell (the report says 112).
- Hard rules kept: the probe labels are only skill_confirmation, train and val.

**Literature**
- metabench is ICLR 2025, with 1.24 % / 0.58 % RMSE and r 0.94 ([ICLR](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/4ebc26584810a189ef1e4f173aba4319-Abstract-Conference.html)).
- PromptEval Eq. 3.2, P(Y_ij = 1) = σ(f_ψ(x_i) − g_γ(z_j)), has no prompt x example interaction ([arXiv HTML](https://arxiv.org/html/2405.17202)).
- Fluid Benchmarking reports 50x fewer items on MMLU.

**Sound and adoptable at zero cost**
- Keep always-pass items (they carry the harm signal).
- Never select items by movability (+7-point bias).
- Never drop items on a 2-run pre-screen (the pilot lost 78 % of the gain that way).
- Declare the estimand of every number.
- Use 2 runs per item.
- Neyman allocation gives a modest, real 7-10 % RMSE reduction (pilot ratio 0.926), but only when subsampling from a larger pool. It gives nothing when a fixed panel is run in full.

**Critic scripts**, in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-dulin-Documents-Paper-SkillOpt/e7258b97-b430-4dd5-959d-eb871e7c777f/scratchpad/feas/E5-critic/:
- c1_gtheory.py
- c2_strata_auc.py
- c3_gate_power.py
- c4_pilot_check.py (streamed over SSH, no remote writes)
- c5_dstudy_checks.py
missing:
1. **No power analysis of the proposed family gate against invalid families.** Done here: it admits 32-77 % of them. A redesign would need many small-effect calibration texts measured against the actual parent, plus larger criterion pools. The cost of that is not estimated.

2. **No analysis with the task-card parent, the owner's yardstick.** cal-1 has no "task card + rule" arm. A cal-1-style fixture is needed (task card + rule-shaped or learned additions + placebos) before any stratum rule, D-study figure or TPS threshold is set for the I-ds chain.

3. **Purpose-2 endpoint design is missing:**
   - MDEs on the evaluation panels;
   - a pooled similar-target endpoint (about 3 points);
   - the key trade-off. The similarity hub, OfficeQA, has the smallest pool: 74 items, gate MDE 9.6 points. SearchQA's 600 items give about 3.0, but it has only one similar target.
   - There is no advice on which benchmark to evolve on.

4. **Conflicts with the owner's rules that need a ruling:**
   - TPS_X uses target benchmarks' training pools to choose evolution-side items, which conflicts with "evolve on one, evaluate on the rest".
   - A fixed real criterion pool for validating generator families is a de-facto fixed validation set for the verifier side.

5. **Session drift is absent from the TPS_F simulation.** The family and the criterion share one cal-1 session. The same text on the same items moved from +8.88 (cal-1) to +6.74 points (v3) across sessions. A family measured later would be falsely rejected more often unless the real pool is re-measured in the same window, at about 3,600 extra cells per validation.

6. **Costs off SearchQA are not given.**
   - A 2,000-cell family gate costs about 9-16M tokens on OfficeQA and about 57-212M on ALFWorld at v3 rates.
   - A 74-item OfficeQA fixture is too noisy (SE about 4-5 points) to serve as the criterion.
   - The 0.80 / ±4 thresholds were calibrated on SearchQA's 200 items and do not transfer.

7. **The SearchQA fresh pool is nearly exhausted.** Never-used training items are down to 59 of 600 (200 focal, 31 regression, 130 D1-v2, 180 E5-P1).

8. **"Items over runs" cannot be followed in most places.** It does not apply to fixed evaluation panels or to the small training pools (OfficeQA 74, ALFWorld 57, SpreadsheetBench 91 judgeable). Only SearchQA (600) and LiveMath (283) can host a 220-370-item gate. Benchmark choice or pooling is the real lever.

9. **The two readings of "coding rubric" were not compared** (executable checks vs text criteria), although the batch-2 context asked for that.

10. **R6 has no pre-specified decision rule** for its per-stratum gain and harm tests. The gain stratum moved between item samples (mixed on the focal panel, 2-run always-fail on fresh items), so choosing it post hoc is a forking path.
notes_cn:
审查结论：部分成立。数字可靠，但两个关键推论和核心新提议站不住。
修正后可行性：低。这里的"低"指这个方向特有的部分，即"按单题或按题目家族挑出能预测泛化的题"。其中几条免费的统计规矩可以马上用，但收益不大，而且和 D8/D11 重叠。

名词说明：
- 技能文本：放进解题模型提示词里的说明。
- 空骨架：没有内容的初始技能。
- 任务卡：各基准公开的解题说明，也就是好的初始指令。
- 父版本：当前在用的技能文本。
- cal-1：校准实验，SearchQA 的 200 道训练题、11 种文本、每种答 4 遍。
- AUC：预测准确度，0.5 等于瞎猜，1 为完美。
- 题目家族：同一出题规则生成的一批题。
- 最小可测效果：有 80% 把握能测出的最小分差。

一、我核对属实的
- 用自己写的程序重算了 cal-1：分差构成（题目本身 64%、文本×题目交叉 12%、文本整体 1.3%、随机 23%）、三层题数（37/52/111）和各层净变化，全部一致。
- 直接读取试点的 1,800 个原始结果重算，也全部一致：
  - 任务卡比空骨架高 8.89 分；
  - 两个有害文本分别低 11.4 分和 8.6 分；
  - 在"预筛两次都对"的题上，两个有害文本各掉约 17 分；
  - 共用 324 万 token。
- 全程没有读任何测试题。

二、站不住的地方
1. 核心新提议"出题家族合格检验"（相关≥0.80、偏差≤4 分）查不出它该查的问题。我按探索者自己的模拟方法加入了不合格的家族：
   - 只对大差别有反应、对 6 个小差别完全没反应的家族，约 64%–66% 能通过；
   - 把所有差别放大 1.46 倍的家族，77% 能通过；
   - 整体偏高 3 分的家族，68% 能通过；
   - 合格的家族反而有 13% 被拒，不是报告说的 5%–10%。
   原因是 9 个校准文本里，3 个大效果文本主导了相关系数。所以这道检验不能保证生成题能测出"学到的规则比任务卡好多少"这种小差别。

2. "生成题在小差别上相关 −0.24、高估约 5 分"不能证明生成题不合格。
   - 真实题那一侧 10 个对比本身的误差（约 2.8 分）比它们彼此之间的差异（约 2.5 分）还大，任何题都不可能和它相关。
   - 只看我们实际使用的 deepseek 解题模型（4 个对比），生成题只高 0.6 分；约 5 分的高估主要来自 GLM 系列模型（高 8.4 分）。
   - 正确的说法是"只有 74 道真实题，现在测不出来"。

3. "AUC 0.85，能事先看出哪些题会被任务卡改善"，这个数字大部分是必然的。
   - 每次都做对的题不可能再提高，只凭"是不是每次都对"这一条就有 0.82。
   - 纯随机波动造成的"假改善题"，用同样方法也能得到 0.79。
   - 试点里只答两遍的预筛版本只有 0.51。

4. "泛化得到验证"会误导。试点验证的是"任务卡比空骨架好"在同一个基准的新题上仍然成立。它不是"一个基准上进化、其他基准上评测"，测的也不是学到的规则。

5. "最小可测泛化效果 6.8–12.2 分"用的是训练题的题量。
   - 按登记的测试题量（SearchQA 400、OfficeQA 172、LiveMath 125、SpreadsheetBench 约 177、ALFWorld 134），用探索者自己的参数算出来分别是 3.7、6.3、7.3、6.5、8.0 分。
   - 如果把几个"相似"基准合成一个总指标，约 3 分。

6. 报告的所有分析都以空骨架为父版本，没有一个是您真正关心的"在任务卡上再加规则"。用最接近的替代对比（在任务卡上再加其余四段说明）估算，所需题量约 200 道，大约是报告所说 374 道的一半。

三、遗漏的问题，有几项需要您决定
- OfficeQA 和另外三个基准都登记为"相似"，最适合做"进化一个、评测其余"的源头。但它只有 74 道训练题，在它上面把关只能测出约 10 分的效果。SearchQA 训练题最多（600 道全部用上约 3 分），却只有 OfficeQA 一个相似目标。
- SearchQA 从未用过的训练题现在只剩 59 道。
- 报告建议用目标基准的训练题来挑选进化用的题，这和"只在一个基准上进化"冲突，需要您决定是否允许。

四、可以马上采用的规矩
- 不删每次都做对的题；
- 不只挑"最容易变的题"，否则会把效果高估约 7 分；
- 不凭两遍预筛删题；
- 每题答两遍，把预算花在更多的题上；
- 每个数字都说明是"对新题"还是"只对这套题"。
家族合格检验要先加入更多小效果的校准文本，并证明能拒绝上面这些不合格的家族，在那之前不能当作"验证端进化"的依据。
